message.title: Message
message.description:
One message on a subscription. `seq` counts the subscription's messages from 1, with no
gaps: a client that sees one asks for a resync.

oneOf.description: Part of the resource as it is now, in order; pages follow each other until `synced`.
The snapshot is whole: what follows are changes to it.
Changes, applied together and in order (never half of them).
Forget what you have: a fresh snapshot follows (`reason`: `behind`, `asked`…).
The resource is no more (an agent was closed); nothing follows.

Op.description: A change to a resource: an ordered list of items, each a JSON object with a string `id`.

oneOf.description: The whole item: it replaces the one with its id, or is added at the end.
Text added to the end of one of an item's string fields (streaming text).
The items' order: these ids first, in this order; ids not here keep theirs, after them.

Bytes added to an item's byte stream (a job's output): `data` (base64) starts at byte
`offset` of it. The item's `offset` says where a follower's copy is: bytes before it
it has already (its screen was made after them) and drops; an op starting past it
means some were missed (a gap: resync). See [`unseen`].

agents.description: The open agents, in the sidebar's order (Notes chats not among them).

cwd.description: the folder it works in (its project's, or a worktree of it)

unseen.description: something new the user hasn't seen

place.description: where in the project it works (a repo, a folder)

options.description: the session's settings (ACP configOptions: {id, name, category, currentValue, options: [{value, name} or groups]}): model, effort…; `set_option`

stalled.description: a turn quiet for 3 minutes, no tool running

looking.description: the user has it in front of them in loom

last_turn.description: {turns, seconds, error, cancelled}: `turns` grows as each ends

unsent.description: {times, count}: queued messages that never went out

projects.description: The projects, in the sidebar's order.

conversation/<agent>.description: An agent's conversation: Agent → turn → entry. Questions are entries `awaiting_user` until answered (`answer`).

kind.description: user, agent, thought, tool, question, notice, turn…; an unknown one is drawn plainly

status.description: pending, streaming, awaiting_user, done, failed, cancelled

turn_id.description: t1, t2…: the turn it belongs to

message.description: the agent's id for it (rewind, forks)

button.description: a notice's button, to `press` (gone once a choice is pressed)

parent.description: the task a tool is part of

markdown.description: a question's detail is Markdown (a plan to approve)

options.description: a permission question's options: {id, name, kind}

usage.description: The account's limits and each agent's context and cost.

parts.description: what fills an agent's context: {name, tokens}

job/<id>.description: A job's terminal: its screen, then `bytes` ops at their offsets (drop what the screen holds; past it, resync). A new run: an `upsert`.

screen.description: base64 terminal bytes drawing its screen

offset.description: the stream's byte the screen is at

settings.description: One item: every setting by its snake_case name; secrets only as `<name>_set`.

vault/<folder>.description: A folder of the notes vault (`vault/`: the top), folders first; it follows the files.

note/<path>.description: One note (or file), as read; it follows the file.

scribe.description: Scribe: what it does, asks, proposes and wrote.

subagent/<agent>/<subagent>.description: A subagent's own conversation (a `crew/<agent>` item's id; a tool entry's `subagent`), entries as an agent's.

crew/<agent>.description: An agent's subagents (tasks it runs), while its turn goes on.

id.description: the subagent's session, or its task's tool call

guessed.description: no session of its own: its state is a guess from its steps

overview.description: What the overview's cards show beside `agents`: people's alone.

waiting.description: the titles of its questions waiting

questions.description: those questions: {entry, title, options: [{id, name, kind}], form} (`answer`; a form in its conversation)

reply.description: the start of its last reply (240 characters, one line)

plan/<agent>.description: Claude's plan for the work (its to-do list), as it last said it.

workflows/<agent>.description: The workflows an agent launched, followed from their files (`stop_workflow`).

state.description: running, failed, stopped, ended, or what it said when done

dir.description: the folder of its agents' transcripts (on loomd's computer)

mcp.description: Each agent's MCP servers, as its process last said.

jobs_shown.description: A job an agent brings forward for the user: a client opens it.

job.description: the job it opened for the user (a login)

inputs.description: What waits in each agent's input: the user's own words, so people's alone (not in `agents`, which agents and bridges read).

draft.description: what waits in its input (a rewind's message, one taken back)

queued.description: its messages waiting for the turn to end, in order (`unqueue`)

suggestion.description: the next message it suggests (Tab takes it)

bridges.description: The bridges as they say they are (Settings shows the same), the pairing ticket aside (`pairing`).

candidate.description: a device asking to pair: {id, name}

pairing.description: The remote bridge's pairing ticket, while pairing is open (`pairing {open}`): whoever has it can ask to pair, so the window's alone.

schedules.description: Scheduled prompts (made by agents' tools or in the window).

title.description: the agent's, when it was made

session.description: the conversation it goes on (none: a new one each time)

asks.description: What agents ask of the user beyond their conversation, where no window of loom's shows it (loomd): a UI shows them; `ask_done`, `ask_open`.

kind.description: open (a file to see), edit (a file to fill in), notify, input (a job waits for the user to type in its terminal: a password, a y/n)

bridge/<name>.description: A bridge's events: each an item added and taken away at once (a snapshot is empty).

send.description: A message to an agent, as typed in its chat. Bridges send no `!` commands.

text.description: the message (text or pictures are needed)

images.description: pictures, base64, any format the UI reads

answer.description: Answers a question waiting in a conversation; the first answer wins (later ones: conflict). Bridges never answer "Always allow"; the CLI answers nothing (but in a test instance, LOOM_TEST_INSTANCE=1).

option.description: a permission question: the chosen option's id

content.description: a form: what was filled in

set_mode.description: An agent's permission mode. `bypassPermissions` from loom's window only.

suspend.description: Suspends an agent (frees its memory; opening it or a message resumes it). A conflict while it works.

set_awake.description: Keeps an agent awake, or lets it be suspended when idle.

awake.description: never suspended for being idle (true), or allowed

changes.description: The files an agent created or changed, with their diffs.
changes.result: {files: [{path, mark: created|changed, repo, status: git's two letters, diff: against the last commit}]}

revert.description: Throws away changes to a file the agent touched, back to the last commit: all of them, or one hunk. It can't be undone. A file git doesn't know (new) is not reverted.

hunk.description: one hunk of that file's diff (from 0); none: the whole file

hunk_text.description: with `hunk`: that hunk as shown, from its @@ line (a conflict if the file's diff has changed there)

fork.description: A copy of the whole conversation, as an agent of its own (it shows in `agents`).

clear.description: /clear: the agent starts a fresh conversation (the old one stays among the past ones).

restart.description: Stops the agent's process and starts it again, resuming its conversation.

add_folder.description: Lets the agent work in another folder too (it restarts).

export.description: The conversation as Markdown: what was said, by whom.

move_agent.description: Moves an agent in the sidebar's order.

by.description: -1 up, 1 down, among its project's agents

move_project.description: Moves a project in the sidebar's order.

mark_seen.description: The user has seen what is new in an agent (or in all): `unseen` goes.

send_now.description: Ctrl+Enter: its queued messages go into the running turn now (or as the next prompt).

stop_workflow.description: Stops a workflow the agent runs.

stop_subagent.description: Stops one subagent (or background task) of the agent's, the rest going on.

mcp_server.description: Connects one of the agent's tool servers (MCP) again, or switches it on or off; `mcp` shows how it went.

reload_extensions.description: The agent's session reads its skills and plugins again (changed in loom's Claude folder).

press.description: Presses a notice's button ("Rewind" with the files…). A choice's button goes once pressed.

rewind.description: A copy of the conversation from just before your message, with it in the input to change; the copy shows in `agents` (this one is kept). With files: the files go back too.

files.description: the files Claude changed from there on too

set_option.description: Changes a session setting of the agent's (the model, the effort…); its `options` say the new one.

set_draft.description: Sets what waits in the agent's input (`inputs`), as a client took or sent it.

unqueue.description: Takes a queued message back into the agent's input (`inputs`).

rename.description: Renames an agent (its own titles don't replace it then).

reopen.description: Reopens a conversation closed lately, as an agent.

past_conversations.description: Claude Code's past conversations, newest first (200 at most).

resume.description: A past conversation picked up as an agent (the one open, if it is).

schedule_new.description: Schedules a prompt for an agent.

same.description: in its conversation (true), or a new one each time

pairing.description: The remote bridge's pairing: its ticket is in `bridges`.

pair_confirm.description: Lets in the device asking to pair, and closes pairing.

id.description: the device shown to the user (`bridges`' candidate)

act.description: run_now, pause (pauses or goes on), remove

loomd_stop.description: loomd stops, as on SIGTERM: agents stopped (their conversations resume next time), the workspace saved. The window restarts an older loomd with it.

set_looking.description: What loom's window shows (loomd: no desktop notice about those agents, none of a question while the window is in use). Said again within a minute, else forgotten.

new_agent.description: Starts an agent in a folder.

set_collapsed.description: Folds a project in the sidebar, or unfolds it (every UI's).

remove_project.description: Takes a project out of the sidebar, closing its agents (they can be reopened). A conflict while any of them works.

close_agent.description: Closes an agent (its conversation resource ends: gone).

run_job.description: A new job in the project's tray.

job_text.description: A job's output as text (to copy).

remove_job.description: Takes a job that has exited out of its tray (a conflict while it runs).

text.description: keys typed, as the terminal sends them (escapes included)

job_resize.description: The size a job's terminal is shown at (one size for every client: the last one told).

restart_job.description: Runs a job again (its output starts over).

set_settings.description: Changes settings. What may send things off this machine, decides what agents may do or names a program loom runs (bridges, pairing, speech to text, the agent program, the default mode, the editor, the notes vault) only from loom's window.

changes.description: settings by their names in `settings`, with new values

query.description: words, all of them in a note

scribe_decide.description: Decides on a change Scribe proposes.

scribe_drop.description: Drops an item from Scribe's lists.

scribe_fix.description: Scribe changes a note it wrote as you say.

said.description: what's wrong or missing ("it's net, not gross")

scribe_teach.description: Tells Scribe why it was wrong.

scribe_history.description: Everything Scribe wrote or was told no, newest first (`scribe_undo` takes a written one back).
scribe_history.result: {changes: [{id, kind: written|dropped, topic, reason, change, title, at, undone}]}

scribe_seen.description: A change Scribe wrote, seen: shown folded from then on.

scribe_check.description: Scribe reads what is left unread of a conversation, now ("Check now").

save.description: A file for an agent, saved in its folder under `<bridge>-files/` (a bridge's) or `web-files/` (dropped in a web page), never over another.

transcribe.description: Speech to text with loom's settings (its key never leaves loom).

bridge_state.description: What the bridge says of itself (any object), shown in Settings.

bridge.description: The bridge protocol, for bridges that still speak it (the remote one, for the phone app already shipped); its events: `bridge/<name>`.

web_open.description: Starts the web page's server (this computer only) if it isn't, and a link to it with a one-time token (two minutes). The page is who opened the link: the window's rights, or the CLI's.

port.description: where to listen on 127.0.0.1 (else any free port), the first time

web_close.description: Stops the web page's server; every page let in is let go.

topics.description: The notes vault's topics (Notes on, with a vault).
topics.result: {vault, topics: [{name, path, folder, listens_for, apply: ask|auto, sync, enabled}]}

topic_set.description: Switches a topic on or off.

topic_new.description: A new topic, its file from loom's template or drafted from `about`.

about.description: what it keeps, in a sentence: Claude drafts its file from it

claude_items.description: The skills, agents and commands only loom's agents load (its Claude folder).
claude_items.result: {folder, items: [{kind: skill|agent|command, name, description, enabled, shipped, path}]}

claude_set.description: Switches one on or off (agents started or woken from now on).

claude_new.description: A new one, from loom's template.

claude_restore.description: Puts back loom's own version of one it ships.

delete_conversation.description: Deletes a past conversation (Claude Code's file of it). It can't be undone.

dirs_list.description: A folder's folders (hidden ones left out), to pick a project's folder.

edit_file.description: Opens the file in the user's editor (the setting, else the desktop's), on this computer.

path.description: a file in a project, a topic's, or one of `claude_items`'

files_list.description: A folder's entries, folders first (.git left out).

files_find.description: Finds a project's files by name (Ctrl+P), best first.

query.description: letters of the path, in order

file_read.description: A file's text (null: not text, or over 2 MB) and when it changed (ms), for `file_write`.

bytes.description: its bytes instead ({data}: base64, 10 MB at most)

path.description: a file in a project (new or not)

modified.description: when it changed as read: a conflict if it changed since

git_repos.description: The project's git repositories and what changed in each (git's two letters: M  staged, ` M` not yet, ?? new).
git_repos.result: {repos: [{path, name, branch, ahead, behind, changes: [{code, file}]}]}

staged.description: the staged changes (else the ones not yet)

git_do.description: Stages, unstages or throws away files' changes, or commits what is staged.

act.description: stage, unstage, discard (back to the last commit: it can't be undone), commit

path.description: a file or folder in a project

how.description: app (its own app: the default), folder (its folder in the file manager)

trash_file.description: Moves it to the desktop's trash (gio trash).

path.description: a file or folder in a project (not the project)

git_show.description: One commit: who, when, its message, the files it changed and its diff (git show).

graph.description: every branch, with the graph drawn before each line

skip.description: the newest ones left out: the next page

git_log.result: {commits: [{graph, hash, refs, subject, author, when, parents}]}

ask_done.description: An ask answered: a file filled in (the agent goes on), or one seen (it goes).

ask_cancel.description: A file the user won't fill in: the agent hears they cancelled; the ask goes.

ask_open.description: Opens an ask's file in the user's editor (the setting, else the desktop's), on this computer.

notes_open.description: loomd: a Notes chat open (an agent working in the vault): its conversation is `conversation/<agent>`.

session.description: a past chat (`notes_chats`); none: a new one

topic.description: a new chat about this topic (`topics`), its notes in reach

notes_close.description: loomd: a Notes chat closed (it stays among the past ones).

tool.description: An agent's loom tools (its MCP server), as the agent loom found the caller to be.

name.description: a loom tool's request (run_job, job_output, open_file, …)
